$comment: separate-pull-requests, so each release PR names its own version. With both packages in one PR release-please cannot fit two versions in one title and falls back to `chore: release main` - the repo went from `chore(main): release 0.2.1` to a title saying nothing. They also release on genuinely independent cadences: the moving v0 tag that every consumer pins, and an npm package. One PR each keeps those decisions separate. always-update, because two PRs share one manifest: both bump adjacent lines of .release-please-manifest.json, so merging one leaves the other conflicting. Without it release-please rebuilds an open PR only when its release notes change, and a release of the other package does not change them - #55 on 2026-09-23 and #76 on 2026-09-24 sat conflicting until rebased by hand. With it every push to main rebuilds each open release PR on that main. The cost: a force push to every release PR per push to main, which re-runs its CI and dismisses an approval given before that push.
